subject.title: feat: per-job elevated exec scoping for cron and heartbeat

question: Should elevated host-exec authority for cron and heartbeat be modeled as narrow per-job/heartbeat approval metadata, or folded into the broader non-forgeable scheduling provenance design?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the permanent authority source, storage shape, audit trail, migration behavior, and fail-closed defaults change a security boundary for existing cron and heartbeat users.

options.title: Fold into scheduling provenance
options.body: Treat elevated execution as part of the broader Gateway-owned schedule authority model so cron creation, mutation, heartbeat provenance, audit, and execution checks share one trust contract.

options.title: Implement narrow elevated markers
options.body: Add per-job and heartbeat-specific elevated approval metadata now, with explicit execution-time checks, docs, and migration behavior.

options.title: Fail closed for internal sources
options.body: Remove wildcard internal-source elevated inheritance by default and require explicit operator opt-in, accepting upgrade friction for current setups.

recommendation.title: Fold into scheduling provenance
recommendation.body: Treat elevated execution as part of the broader Gateway-owned schedule authority model so cron creation, mutation, heartbeat provenance, audit, and execution checks share one trust contract.

likelyOwner.reason: They most recently owned the adjacent cron caller-scope implementation across the Gateway, protocol, and agent cron tool paths that this decision would extend.
